title: M1: Vault browse (portable vault, part 1)
description:
Milestone M1 from roadmap.md: browse your REAL Bitwarden vault on the T-Embed color device.

Done when: unlock/browse your real vault on the color device (list + detail views), backed by companion-app push of real (decrypted) credentials.

Two pillars (largely parallel):
- Pillar A (on-device UI): credential list refinements + a new detail view designed for color + rotary encoder. M0 left on_activate unset in core/src/app.rs and explicitly deferred the detail view to M1/Uma. Also must solve the flagged problem: a sync landing mid-navigation must not blow away a pushed detail screen.
- Pillar B (companion app): a real companion that runs the Bitwarden SDK, authenticates, syncs, decrypts, and pushes real VaultItems over the existing HTTP+CBOR /api/sync push path (PushSyncSource already exists). Roadmap sanctions a CLI or simple desktop GUI for testing; full Web Vault integration deferred post-M2.

Kickoff phase = design (advisory, read-only): Uma (UX for list+detail), Ada (companion-app architecture + sync-vs-pushed-screen design), Fern (detail-view framework integration). Implementation children created after designs land.

title: M1: extract push-protocol wire crate
description: Extract Credential/SyncRequest/SyncResponse out of emulator/src/credentials into a new host-only push-protocol crate (serde + ciborium + uuid; NO dependency on bhk-core). Both emulator and the new companion depend on it so the CBOR /api/sync contract is defined once and cannot drift. From<Credential> for VaultItem stays in emulator (the only place that sees both crates). Per Ada's M1 architecture report.

title: M1: companion app - bw-CLI bridge
description: Host-only companion crate that bridges the official Bitwarden CLI (bw) to the device push path: shell out to bw list items, deserialize JSON, filter to login items (type==1), map to Credential (name, username, login.password, login.uris[0]->uri, notes, id), CBOR-encode a SyncRequest, POST to /api/sync. Depends on push-protocol for wire types + serde_json + a small blocking HTTP client (ureq). Verify field mapping against a real bw list items dump before finalizing. Record deliberate M1 omissions (totp, reprompt, folders, extra URIs). Per Ada's report; recommended over full Rust-SDK companion for time-to-real-data and demo credibility.

title: M1: VaultStore data model + no-rebuild App::step
description: Foundation for the M1 UI. Introduce a shared, App-owned VaultStore (items + SyncStatus) exposed to domain widgets via Rc<RefCell>, replacing the M0 shortcut where App::step rebuilds the whole Navigator on every sync (core/src/app.rs:92-100) and where VaultItem->ListItem drops the id (app.rs:18-20). App::step becomes: pull latest snapshot, write into store, set dirty on change - and NEVER rebuild the Navigator. Safe because step (borrow_mut) and render (borrow) are strictly sequential phases of the run loop, single-threaded. SyncStatus for M1 derived in App from sync() Result + item count (Synced/Error/Empty); richer Syncing/Offline deferred (no SyncSource trait change). GATED on the vault-store-data-ownership ADR. Per Fern's framework report (B1).

title: M1: CredentialListView (store-backed, activate->detail)
description: Domain list widget reading the VaultStore live: selection tracked by VaultItem id (re-resolve to index after a store change, clamp if id vanished, so a background sync does not jump the cursor). on_activate builds the detail Screen bound to the selected id + store handle. Content-region empty/syncing/error states from store status + item count. Right-edge scrollbar. Full-row focus fill + 3px left accent bar (shared draw_focus_block helper). Retires the ad-hoc list + id-dropping projection in app.rs. Per Uma (UX) + Fern (B2).

title: M1: dynamic chrome (title/readout/status dot/contextual hint)
description: Add a Widget::chrome_contribution hook (title override, position readout, contextual hint) merged by Screen::render over the static title/hint. Thread app-global SyncStatus into render for a title-bar status dot. Slotted title bar: clip the title to its sub-rect (retire the un-clipped single-blob title at screen.rs:157-162) and right-align the 3/42 readout using font metrics, not a hardcoded px/char (survives the later u8g2-fonts swap). Per Fern (B3) + Uma. Depends on the VaultStore foundation; readout/hint sources land with the list/detail widgets.

title: M1: CredentialDetailView + SecretField (new detail screen)
description: New single-container detail view (Flavor 2: one focusable widget managing field focus internally, so it dodges the both-fire navigator footgun and can render a cohesive gone-state). Fields: USERNAME, PASSWORD, WEBSITE (if Some), NOTES (if Some), read live from the store by id. SecretField: masked as a fixed count of dots (not true length - no length leak), amber cleartext when revealed, reveal toggled on Activate, auto re-mask on FocusEvent::Lost. Field focus clamps (not wraps). Deleted-upstream -> store.get(id)==None -> gentle 'no longer in your vault' state with Back. Reserve (do NOT build) a per-field slot for M2 type-over-HID. Per Uma (UX) + Fern (B4).

title: M1: end-to-end verification (real bw vault -> device browse)
description: Tess: prove the M1 done-condition end to end. Run the companion against a real bw-unlocked vault, push over /api/sync, and browse list + detail on the device in headless (agent-driven, screenshot-inspected) and windowed (screencapture) modes. Verify: list renders real credentials, activate opens detail, password reveal/re-mask works, Back returns with selection preserved, and a re-push mid-detail does not yank the user out. Zoomed/live inspection per rendering-verification discipline. Real-hardware run folds into the on-hardware verification bead when boards arrive.

title: On-device first-class client via PRIVATE FORK of Bitwarden SDK (DEFERRED)
description:
DEFERRED / backlog. Revive ONLY if the companion-push concept validates and on-device decrypt is still wanted. Direction: PRIVATE fork (NOT upstream) -- rationale (Andreas, 2026-08-11): side project; feature-flag swaps for embedded impls likely never ship in production, so it should not add cost to Bitwarden's real SDK.

Requires solving THREE independent fronts (per spike ai-bitwarden-hw-key-8d7.2):
1. SDK non-modularity + transport: fork bitwarden-api-base/-core/-key-connector to inject an esp-idf/mbedtls transport (no seam today; they use reqwest::Client directly). Also feature-gate bitwarden-api-key-connector out of bitwarden-crypto so 'just the KDF' is depend-able.
2. ring-on-xtensa (NOT fixed by forking BW crates): ring's bundled C crypto links wrong-endian on xtensa-esp32s3-espidf (build.rs target detection). Options: patch ring's build.rs, or swap rustls to a pure-Rust RustCrypto crypto provider to drop ring (unverified on xtensa).
3. On-hardware validation: footprint (512KB SRAM / 8MB PSRAM), real PBKDF2/Argon2id latency, session-key fast path -- ALL still unmeasured (no physical board during the spike).

Reference artifact: throwaway spike branch 'bd-ai-bitwarden-hw-key-8d7.2' (pushed to origin) contains spike-sdk/ with the minimal repro + exact mitigations (ring 'less-safe-getrandom-espidf' feature; opt-level=0 for rustls/mockall). DO NOT delete that branch.

title: Add test coverage to bhk-core (currently green-by-absence)
description: Tess flagged during W2 verify: cargo test runs clean but has 0 test cases across all suites. Not a regression, but the workspace has no real assertions. Add unit tests as core logic (VaultItem, render core, input model) lands in W3+.

title: Fix host-build ergonomics: workspace default target esp32s3 forces --target everywhere
description:
Since W6 set .cargo/config.toml [build] target = xtensa-esp32s3-espidf as the WORKSPACE default, every host command (cargo build/test/run/clippy for emulator + bhk-core) fails unless you pass --target aarch64-apple-darwin (minifb/tiny_http can't cross-compile to xtensa; and cargo run would try espflash). Multiple agents + the user have tripped on this; the .cargo/config.toml comment wrongly claims the emulator is 'unaffected'. 

Fix options to weigh: (a) move the esp32s3 default into firmware/.cargo/config.toml (per-dir) and leave the workspace root defaulting to host, so / and  'just work' and firmware builds from its dir or with explicit --target; (b) add cargo aliases (e.g. ) ; (c) keep global esp32s3 but fix the misleading comment + document the --target requirement prominently in README. Recommend (a): day-to-day dev is the emulator, so the ergonomic default should be host. Also correct the false comment at .cargo/config.toml:5-6.

title: M0: Platform Migration (T-Embed color + rotary, hardware-portable foundation)
description:
Green-field rebuild of the UI framework + app architecture for the Lilygo T-Embed (ESP32-S3, 320x170 color ST7789, rotary encoder), hardware-portable, first-class-Bitwarden-client direction. Synthesizes Ada's architecture design and Fern's UI-framework design.

KEY DECISIONS (orchestrator-reconciled from Ada + Fern):
- Platform-free 'core' crate; hardware injected behind a Platform boundary (Display/Input/Clock/Storage).
- Single generic main loop replaces the two divergent loops (main.rs vs bin/desktop.rs).
- Shared in-RAM Rgb565 framebuffer is the single render output; 3 run modes differ only at final flush -> headless screenshot faithful to device by construction.
- Rgb565 canonical throughout core (RESOLVED conflict: Ada proposed RGB888; Fern's Rgb565 wins for 3-mode fidelity). Core bound to Error=Infallible; mipidsi error absorbed at device surface.
- Retire BOTH GUI engines: src/gui/ is dead code (all call sites commented out); src/simple_gui/ custom RGBA rasterizer blocks color. Salvage concepts only (nav stack, ComponentAction, FocusEvent) reimplemented on embedded-graphics.
- Rotary-encoder NavIntent vocabulary (Next/Prev/NextN/Activate/Back) replaces 3-button KeyCode. Encoder-only for the M0 shell; keep intent seam for future button driver.
- SyncSource seam decouples app from the SDK spike; PushSyncSource (existing HTTP+CBOR) is fallback/dev aid, SdkSyncSource behind the spike.
- OSS: adopt embedded-graphics + embedded-graphics-framebuf + mipidsi + u8g2-fonts + light embedded-layout; defer embedded-menu to M1; reject slint/lvgl and SDL2 simulator.

DONE WHEN (roadmap.md M0): empty-but-real 320x170 color shell, encoder-drivable, running identically in all three modes (headless/windowed/real-target); SDK spike delivers a go/no-go + ADR.

title: W1: Freeze core interfaces (Platform/Surface/Framebuffer/InputEvent/Clock/Storage) + NavIntent + record ADRs
description: Joint Ada+Fern interface freeze -> ADR-ready. Freeze: Framebuffer (in-RAM Rgb565, embedded-graphics-framebuf), DisplaySurface (flushes framebuffer; Error=Infallible in core, mipidsi error at device adapter), InputSource + rotary InputEvent, NavIntent enum {Next,Prev,NextN(u16),Activate,Back}, Clock, Storage (opaque-blob KV), Platform capability bundle, SyncSource seam. Gates almost everything. Output: ADRs (surface/run-mode seam; portability+workspace; input model; sync-source seam; UI-framework reuse-vs-rewrite) + updated INDEX/progress/roadmap.

title: W8: SDK feasibility spike (throwaway) — build/link, footprint, KDF latency, session-key fast path
description: PARALLEL, START NOW, gates M1 sync DIRECTION not the M0 shell. Throwaway spike bin/branch. Prove: (1) Bitwarden Rust SDK dep tree builds/links for xtensa-esp32s3-espidf — top unknown is TLS (rustls/ring vs esp-idf mbedtls) and async runtime (tokio on esp-idf); (2) footprint fits ~512KB SRAM + 8MB PSRAM; (3) KDF/unlock latency measured on-device (PBKDF2 600k, Argon2id) — the UX gate; (4) session-key fast-path prototype (full unlock once -> wrap+persist session key -> re-unlock cheap). Output: go/no-go + measurements + ADR. NOT merged firmware.

title: W2: Workspace restructure — extract platform-free 'core' crate; migrate credential model to VaultItem
description: Split single crate into workspace: core (lib, no platform deps), firmware (esp bin), emulator (host bin). Makes the portable-core boundary compiler-enforced instead of convention (today core can 'use esp_idf_svc' and only fail on host build). Migrate src/credentials/mod.rs into core as a VaultItem view-model (projection from any SyncSource), decoupled from push-CBOR Credential and SDK Cipher.

title: W3: Render core + UI framework on embedded-graphics (Rgb565 framebuffer, Widget/Action/FocusEvent, nav stack)
description: Fern's core deliverable. Retire src/gui/ (dead) + src/simple_gui/ RGBA rasterizer. Reimplement on embedded-graphics + embedded-graphics-framebuf: retained-mode Widget trait {measure, render(area, &mut Surface), is_focusable, on_focus, on_intent}; Action = PushView/PopView/Back/None; Navigator owns screen stack (salvage simple_gui/document nav-stack + focus memory); region layout (title/content/hint bars) + linear stacks, light embedded-layout; true clipping via DrawTargetExt::clipped() (retire char-skip marquee); u8g2-fonts foreground-colored text (retire baked leaked mono fonts + '?'-fallback bug). Depends on W1 interface freeze; UI-framework reuse-vs-rewrite ADR is part of W1.

title: W9: SyncSource trait + PushSyncSource (wrap existing HTTP+CBOR push)
description: Introduce SyncSource {sync()->Vec<VaultItem>, unlock(secret)} so App never names the SDK or HTTP server directly. PushSyncSource wraps the demoted-but-working HTTP+CBOR push (src/desktop/http_server.rs, Arc<Mutex<Vec<Credential>>>). SdkSyncSource is developed behind W8. This is the decoupling that de-gates M0/M1 from the spike outcome.

title: W4: Host surface adapters — MinifbSurface, HeadlessSurface(PNG), host Clock, file Storage
description: Host adapters flushing the shared Rgb565 framebuffer. MinifbSurface: Rgb565->ARGB8888->minifb (from bin/desktop.rs). HeadlessSurface: keep last frame in RAM, PNG-encode on demand for screenshot capture, no window. Host Clock; file Storage (from src/desktop/storage.rs). One host binary, surface chosen at runtime (--headless flag) so both stay compiled and cannot drift; exact ergonomics are Tess's call.

title: W6: T-Embed board adapter — St7789Surface (mipidsi), rotary InputSource, esp Clock, NVS Storage, BoardConfig pin map
description: Real-target adapter. St7789Surface via mipidsi (add mipidsi + display-interface-spi; keep ssd1306 only until parity proven, then drop). Rotary-encoder driver producing NavIntent. esp Clock; NVS-backed Storage. BoardConfig pin map + peripheral init live ONLY here (today hardcoded in src/main.rs:47-115).

title: W5: Headless input-injection + screenshot protocol (extend http_server.rs)
description: Extend the existing SyncServer HTTP endpoints so the agent harness injects NavIntent (NOT raw hardware) and captures PNG screenshots from HeadlessSurface. Hardware-agnostic test path. Co-owned Ruby + Tess.

title: W7: Unified Platform-generic main loop; wire all three modes; delete old engines (closes M0)
description: Single run<P: Platform>() loop (input.poll -> app.handle_input -> app.step -> if dirty: display.present(app.render) -> clock.sleep). Wire headless/windowed/real-target. Build the region layout + scrolling-list widget (viewport auto-scroll, true clipping) = the empty-but-real encoder-drivable color shell. Delete src/gui/ + src/simple_gui/ at parity. This is M0 done-when.

title: Fix: windowed emulator renders a blank window (no per-frame minifb update)
description:
SEVERITY: M0 emulator shell is unusable in windowed mode (the human-facing mode). Follow-up to W7 (ai-bitwarden-hw-key-8d7.9).

VISUAL PROOF: launched `./target/aarch64-apple-darwin/debug/desktop` (windowed) from main, screencaptured — the 'Bitwarden HW Key - Desktop Emulator' window opens but renders COMPLETELY BLANK (uniform dark; no Vault title bar, list, or hint bar). The same App renders correctly via HeadlessSurface PNG, so App/render/framebuffer are fine — this is windowed-present-only.

ROOT CAUSE: nothing calls minifb Window::update() per frame. WindowedInput::poll() (emulator/src/platform/input.rs:71-86) reads is_key_down()/get_scroll_wheel() WITHOUT first calling window.update() (minifb requires update() to refresh input state AND to pump/paint the window). MinifbSurface::flush() (minifb_surface.rs:100-109) calls update_with_buffer() but only on dirty frames (run.rs:72). So the window gets a single update_with_buffer on frame 1 and is never pumped again -> macOS never composites it -> blank; input is also dead.

FIX (confined to emulator; do NOT change bhk_core::run or the Platform traits): call window.update() every frame in windowed mode. Cleanest is in WindowedInput::poll(): borrow_mut, window.update(), then read is_key_down/get_scroll_wheel (this is also correct minifb usage - update() must precede input reads). MinifbSurface::flush() continues pushing new pixels via update_with_buffer on dirty frames. Frame 1: poll's update() (empty), then dirty flush's update_with_buffer shows the shell; subsequent frames: poll's update() keeps it alive + responsive.

VERIFICATION: orchestrator (main thread, has Screen Recording permission) relaunches the windowed binary and screencaptures to confirm the Vault shell renders + selection moves on arrow keys. Subagents cannot see a window, so windowed-visual verification is an orchestrator responsibility going forward (relates to bead ai-bitwarden-hw-key-dvm / three-mode testability).

title: Adopt u8g2-fonts in render core (replace MonoFont FONT_6X10)
description: W3 shipped with embedded-graphics' built-in MonoFont FONT_6X10 (ADR-sanctioned as a start). Upgrade to u8g2-fonts for real glyph coverage (fixes the bullet/Unicode gap that made passwords render as '????' in the old prototype) and better legibility on 320x170. Isolated change per the ui-framework ADR (import swap, no Widget API change). Uma should weigh in on font choice as part of M1 visual conventions.

title: Real-target (on-device) verification strategy — DEFERRED until T-Embed ships
description: The real device is NOT directly agent-controllable the way headless/windowed emulator modes are (agent can't physically turn the rotary encoder or read the ST7789 framebuffer). The three-mode ADR's 'real-target' mode needs a concrete verify path. Likely direction to evaluate: reuse the SAME seams the headless mode uses — NavIntent injection + framebuffer capture — but transport them over serial/USB so an agent can drive the physical device and read back its Rgb565 framebuffer as a PNG for visual verification. Alternatives to weigh: on-device serial logging of UI state (text), a framebuffer-dump-over-serial, an on-device self-test mode, or human-in-the-loop (photograph screen + manual encoder). Owners: Tess (three run modes) + Ruby (firmware seam), input from Ada/Fern on the seam. REVISIT when the physical T-Embed arrives (hardware in transit). Blocks fully closing M0's 'drivable on the T-Embed' done-criterion.

title: Firmware: support both T-Embed variants (plain + CC1101)
description: Support both ordered boards behind a build-time board-config selection. Plain T-Embed (primary): encoder A/B/BTN on GPIO2/GPIO1/GPIO0. T-Embed CC1101: encoder on GPIO4/GPIO5/GPIO0 plus an independent user button on GPIO6 (candidate for a dedicated Back later). App/UI stays board-agnostic via NavIntent; this is pin-map + optional extra-button plumbing only, no runtime auto-detection. Firmware GPIO0 = encoder press is also the ESP32-S3 BOOT strap (hold-during-power-on enters download mode) - account for this in any hold-to-X UX. Build-only until physical boards arrive; real verification folds into the on-hardware verification effort. Sources captured in research: LilyGo factory pin_config.h (plain) and T-Embed-CC1101 utilities.h/pinmap.
